newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Short-term pullback possible.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Short-term pullback possible.

text.p: Some indications that the stock market's dizzying run into record ground may be running out of gas emerged in last week's options trading, but analysts remain sanguine on the market's longer term outlook.
Despite increased chances of a short-term pullback, the market's longer-term prospects remain strong, analysts said.
Helping the bullish case is the fact that put buying continues to outpace call buying, a sign that investors remain somewhat cautious.
"Over the first six days after the last expiration, the OEX S&P 100 index .OEX was down 16-1/2 points and from there it rallied 40 points," said Jerry Hegarty at Thomson Financial Services.
"So the fact we're down a couple points here is really no big deal," he said.
At 1140 CST (1740 GMT), the OEX was down 2.34 points at 710.25, off its 709.27 session low.
Trading overall was sluggish as participants caught their breath after Friday's hectic session where the expiration of November contracts bloated volume.
